text:
maya: quick update — ran a mixed SmoothQuant + AWQ sweep on the new 13B model with 64k/128k/200k contexts using the longspan dataset. spotted a consistent quality dip at 128k when AWQ is enabled on later blocks. results look noisy but reproducible.

sam: how big is the dip? numbers plz

maya: short summary:
```
configs: [SQ-only, AWQ-only, SQ+AWQ-mix]
metric: avg_exact_match, rougeL, ppl
64k: SQ-only EM 0.752, rougeL 0.621, ppl 14.2
64k: AWQ-only EM 0.749, rougeL 0.619, ppl 14.5
128k: SQ-only EM 0.743, rougeL 0.613, ppl 15.1
128k: AWQ-only EM 0.741, rougeL 0.610, ppl 15.5
128k: SQ+AWQ-mix EM 0.732 (-1.1 pts vs SQ-only), rougeL 0.598 (-0.015), ppl 16.8
200k: SQ-only EM 0.738, SQ+AWQ-mix EM 0.736 (small drop)
notes: the big delta is specifically for the mixed quant path at 128k; p99 latency comparable.
```

liam: hmm — that smells like activation-tail clipping/scale mismatch when AWQ sees long KV contexts. AWQ per-channel scaling expects activation distribution similar to calibration data. with long tails from longctx, the quant bins compress important mass.

jordan: do we have the calibration configs? maybe the AWQ calibration used short sequences only?

maya: yes, AWQ calibration used default calib set (2k sequences, mostly <8k tokens). i ran a follow-up where we include longtrace examples into calibration and that partially recovered ~0.6 pts of EM. still short of SQ-only.

liam: propose two experiments: (1) actscale multiplier sweep during calib (0.6..1.4, step 0.1) and (2) selective AWQ application: only apply AWQ to first N transformer blocks (e.g., N=18) and keep later blocks SQ'd. hypothesis: later blocks accumulate KV cache tail mass and AWQ causes heavy distortion.

maya: agreed. stacking both improved recovery on a quick local run. here's the minimal runner we used (for infra):
```
./run_quant_bakeoff \
  --model redwood/13b-longctx \
  --ctx-lens 64k,128k,200k \
  --quant-profile "sq_then_awq_mix" \
  --awq-calib-samples 2000 \
  --awq-actscale-sweep "0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9,1.0,1.1" \
  --awq-apply-blocks "0:18" \
  --seed 42
```

benchbot: job 2245123460 started: bench-cluster/jobid=qc-2245-13b-sq-awqmix, estimated 3h

sam: for the writeup — please record per-layer AWQ quant error (L2 on activations) and also capture prefix-reuse rate from the longspan traces. we should check correlation.

maya: noted. will add per-layer error dump and prefix metrics.

liam: minor thought — also try act-aware clipping (per-channel percentile) instead of global multiplier. AWQ is sensitive to outliers so a 99.9th vs 99.99th cutoff could flip results.

jordan: also add a fallback policy in runtime: if mixed-quant path yields lower-quality evals above threshold on validation set, route to SQ-only model for those requests (can be region/latency-tagged).

maya: agree. I'll draft a canary: 10% traffic to mixed-quant, monitor EM and rougeL over 1h windows, auto-fallback if EM drops >0.8 pts for two windows.

sam: thanks — prioritize the calib-sweep and selective-block experiments. please post the per-layer CSVs here when bench finishes.

maya: will do. attaching quick notes link: https://redwood-internal/notebooks/longctx-sq-awq-mix (private) :paperclip:

benchbot: job 2245123460 completed: status=partial-success, artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/qc-2245-13b-sq-awqmix (logs + per-layer-errs.csv)

maya: uploaded csvs and a tiny grafana dashboard snapshot. early read: AWQ per-layer L2 spikes at blocks 19..28 on 128k traces. saving reproducer and starting the actscale sweep now.

sam: cool. once sweep completes let's compare deploy profiles (latency/cost delta) vs SQ-only and put recommendation in the onboarding checklist for 13B-longctx.

liam: FYI i pushed a tiny helper script for per-layer clipping into //eng-ml/tools/awq_calib_helpers.py — use the flag --use-perchannel-clip.

maya: thanks, i'll use it in the next run and post results.

jordan: ETA on full sweep?

maya: estimated 6h for the parameter grid on dedicated bench nodes. i'll ping when done.
